resources.string: Menus, buttons and dates all follow this. It starts on your phone\'s language and stays on whatever you pick.

string-array.name: quips_morning
string-array.item: Let\'s get those hands dusty.
The floor isn\'t going to pour itself.
Coffee first. Then chemistry.
Somewhere out there, a slab is waiting.
Measure twice, mix once.
Today\'s forecast: dust, with a chance of overtime.
Concrete doesn\'t care that you\'re tired.
New day, same ratios.
Boots on, brain on.
Let\'s make something flat and permanent.
The bags won\'t lift themselves — but the maths is done.
Straight lines, strong coffee.

string-array.name: quips_afternoon
string-array.item: Half the day gone, half the floor to go.
Keep moving — pot life is shorter than your patience.
Second wind, second coat.
The client will change their mind at half four. Plan accordingly.
Nothing cures faster just because you\'re in a hurry.
Afternoon: where the words \"quick job\" go to die.
Closer to done than you were this morning.
Mix it right and you only do it once.
Dust now, satisfaction later.
That slab won\'t level itself.
Still standing? Good. Keep going.
Push on — the kettle isn\'t going anywhere.

string-array.name: quips_evening
string-array.item: Tools down soon. Numbers first.
Log it now, or forget it forever.
Long day. Straight lines anyway.
Nearly there — resist the urge to eyeball it.
Tomorrow\'s you would love it if today\'s you wrote it down.
The floor stays. The ache fades.
Wrapping up? Get the usage logged.
Last mix of the day — make it count.
Good work. Now go clean the mixer.
Evening maths beats morning guesswork.
One more coat, or call it a day?
Finish strong, finish flat.

string-array.name: quips_night
string-array.item: Still up? So is the concrete.
Night shift maths, same as day shift maths.
Nobody pours at this hour by choice.
Quiet site, clean mix.
Overtime: sets faster than the sealer.
Go home. The slab will still be there tomorrow.
Late one. Get the ratios right anyway.
The only thing curing right now is you, slowly.
Sleep is a consumable. Budget accordingly.
Mixing at this hour? Double-check that pot life.
Tomorrow starts in a worryingly small number of hours.
Dark outside, level inside.

How to set up a server

If the company ever needs to keep its data somewhere else — a new website, another Google account — set up the new server first, then move everything there from here. Every phone follows by itself; nobody needs a new code.
That server already holds a company. A move needs an empty server.
The old server stops taking changes, everything is copied to the new one, and every phone switches over the next time it connects. Keep the app open until it says it’s done.
Taking everything from the old server…
Sending everything to the new server…
Done. The company is on the new server, and the other phones follow when they next connect. Remove the old server once they all have.
Company moved to a new server?

The server is where the company’s data is kept. It is set up once, on a computer, in about 15 minutes, and after that everything happens in the app. It costs nothing, and the data stays in the company’s own account. Pick one:
Send the server file to myself
Send the website files to myself
On this phone, tap the button below and send the server file to your own email.
On a computer, sign in to the company’s Google account (its Gmail), open script.google.com and click New project.
Open the file from your email, select everything in it (Ctrl+A) and copy it (Ctrl+C). In the project, delete what is already written there, paste (Ctrl+V) and save with the disk button.
At the top, next to Run, pick “prepare” from the list and press Run.

Google asks for permission. Click Review permissions and choose the account. A page says “Google hasn’t verified this app” — that is normal for something you made yourself. Click Advanced, then Go to … (unsafe), then Allow.
Click Deploy → New deployment. Click the gear next to “Select type” and choose Web app.

The two settings that matter — check them both before you click Deploy: Execute as: Me, and Who has access: Anyone (plain “Anyone”, not “Anyone with a Google account”). If this is missed, the app can’t reach the server. It can be fixed later without a new address: Deploy → Manage deployments → pencil.
Copy the Web app URL — it ends in /exec — and send it to your phone (email or a message to yourself).
Back in MixMaster, paste that address where it asks for the server address.

The data is kept in a Google Sheet called “MixMaster data” in that account’s Drive — look, but don’t edit it. If the script is ever changed, publish it with Deploy → Manage deployments → pencil → New version, so its address stays the same.
On this phone, tap the button below and send the website files to your own email.
On a computer, save the zip file from the email and unzip it. Inside is a folder called “mixmaster”.
Log in to the website’s hosting control panel (where the website and domain are paid for) and open the File Manager.
Open the website’s main folder — usually called public_html, htdocs or www — and upload the whole “mixmaster” folder into it.
Open your-website/mixmaster/api.php in a browser. It should say “The server is running and waiting to be set up.”
Back in MixMaster, enter your-website/mixmaster as the server address.

It needs hosting that runs PHP — nearly all do; website builders like Wix or Squarespace don’t. The address must start with https:// (the padlock); if it doesn’t, switch on the free certificate (Let’s Encrypt) in the control panel.
That is the test address (it ends in /dev). Use the Web app URL that ends in /exec: Deploy → Manage deployments.
That is the address of the script editor. The one to use is the Web app URL from Deploy → Manage deployments — it ends in /exec.
Google asks for a sign-in, so the server isn’t open to the app. Deploy → Manage deployments → pencil → Who has access: Anyone (not “Anyone with a Google account”) → Deploy.
The server doesn’t have the MixMaster code in it yet — it was deployed before the code was pasted or saved. Save the code, then Deploy → Manage deployments → pencil → Version: New version → Deploy.
